svg.text: Gift Tracker – Entity relationship design (without preferences)
6 tables: profiles, friend connections, occasions, gifts and gift groups for splitting · normalised to third normal form (3NF)
Arrow points from the parent to the table holding the foreign key
PK primary key · FK foreign key · UK unique key (“composite” = unique across several columns together) 1 · 0..1 · 0..N · 1..N = how many rows on that end
Keys and how duplicates are avoided
• Every table has a primary key (a surrogate id) and every relationship is a foreign key to the parent’s primary key.
• Unique keys stop duplicate rows: one account per email, one gift group per gift, a person joins a group once, the same
two people are connected once, and an occasion is unique per recipient, name and date.
• Each fact is stored once (3NF): a gift’s recipient comes from its occasion (not stored again on the gift); a gift is a
group gift when a gift_group points to it (no isgroupgift flag); a group’s owner is its member with role “owner” (no
• Table names avoid PostgreSQL reserved words: profile instead of user, gift_group instead of group.
Rules enforced by checks and the API
• status, type and role only accept set values: connection status is pending or accepted; occasion type is birthday, christmas, anniversary or
other; gift status is idea, planned, bought or given; role is owner or viewer.
• You can’t send a connection request to yourself (requesterid ≠ addresseeid), and a request A→B also blocks B→A (unique index on the pair,
• price is 0 or more. Every gift belongs to an occasion – use type “other” for a gift without a special day.
• The buyer can’t be the gift’s recipient, and a gift group has exactly one member with role “owner” (checked by the API).
